historical_growth.growth_rate_source: owner_fcf_3yr_cagr (FY2022-FY2025, 3.1%) cross-checked against the pre-COVID-to-now revenue CAGR (FY2019-FY2025, 1.9%) and the RevPAR-led run-rate; both bracket ~2.5-3.5% nominal for a no-acquisition portfolio.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 5-year CAGRs are meaningless: FY2020 is the COVID trough (revenue $1,620M, EBITDA negative, EPS -1.04), so the 30.4% 5-yr revenue CAGR is recovery arithmetic, and EPS 5-yr is undefined. Equity CAGR (~0%) is also not a growth signal for a REIT that distributes >90% of taxable income and buys back stock; it is not used. Owner-FCF series (EBITDA - SBC - cash tax - total capex): FY2019 699, FY2022 812, FY2023 776, FY2024 738, FY2025 889.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR (3.1%) is below the reported-EBITDA 3-yr CAGR (4.7%) because total capex rose from $621M (FY2022) to $724M (FY2025) with the Hyatt/Marriott transformational programs and hurricane reconstruction; the capex burden, not SBC (0.4% of revenue), is what separates reported from owner cash flow at Host.

scenario_narratives.base: Host stays a rate-led luxury/upper-upscale portfolio. FY2026 lands at the twice-raised guidance (~$6.26B revenue, 27.4% EBITDA margin, Adjusted EBITDAre $1.865B) but that year carries the World Cup, America 250, the Maui recovery and low-margin condo sales, so FY2027 slows to +2.5% revenue (about 2% organic plus the two October 2026 acquisitions annualising) and gives back ~30bps of margin; margins then hold at ~27%, where Host has sat in every normal year since FY2016. Revenue grows ~3% to 2030, fading to 2.5%. All capex (R&R plus the brand-mandated Hyatt/Marriott ROI programs, ~9-10% of revenue) is charged; cash taxes stay at the TRS level because REIT status is permanent. Unlevered owner FCF runs ~$1.0-1.1B, discounted at a 9% USD WACC with 2.5% terminal growth. Net debt of $4.1B is pro forma for the Q3 dividend and the $374M spent on Brooklyn Bridge and Plano.
scenario_narratives.bull: The luxury travel cycle extends. Affluent leisure and group demand keep rate growing 4-5% against a luxury pipeline that is effectively closed, the renovated Hyatt and Marriott assets earn their RevPAR premiums, Maui completes its recovery, and margins expand ~120bps to 28.5% as rate outruns wage inflation. Capex normalises toward 9% of revenue once the transformational programs finish. The stock re-rates toward the ~12-13x EV/EBITDA that private buyers paid Host for its own dispositions.
scenario_narratives.bear: The expansion ends in 2027. A consumer or corporate-travel slowdown hits the most cyclical REIT subsector: revenue falls 8% then 4%, and because Host bears the full hotel P&L (no fixed leases) the EBITDA margin compresses to 22% - about half the FY2007-09 damage. Brand standards keep capex from being cut far. Recovery from 2029 returns margins to 26%, 100bps below today, as labour, property-tax and coastal insurance costs reset higher; climate event risk in Maui and Florida remains live. Net debt of $4.1B at ~5.2-year maturity after the October 2026 facility recast means no solvency risk, but distributions and buybacks pause.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Host is valued as what it is: an owner of ~75 luxury and upper-upscale hotels whose cash flow is hotel EBITDA less the heavy, non-optional renovation capex those flags demand. The DCF is unlevered at a 9% USD WACC with every dollar of capex charged and REIT-level (near-zero) cash tax held permanently; net debt is pro forma for the October 2026 dividend and acquisitions, JV stakes are added at book and OP units deducted. AFFO capitalisation was considered and rejected because Host's Adjusted FFO is pre-capex; a FAD-at-cost-of-equity cross-check lands within a dollar of the base case. The value is dominated by the terminal multiple, so the honest readings are the implied EV/EBITDA and the required-return table rather than the point estimate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cyclicality: the bear case models a 2027-28 downturn at half the FY2007-09 severity; a full repeat (revenue -21%, margin 18%) is outside the bear path
Capex assumption: charging ROI capex with only ~3% revenue growth may understate the return on the Hyatt/Marriott programs (upside) or, if brand standards escalate, overstate free cash (downside)
Terminal multiple: the base case implies ~10x EV/EBITDA versus 12-16x paid in private transactions - the model does not credit a re-rating
Concentrated resort-market event risk (Maui wildfire 2023, Florida hurricanes 2024, Hawaii Kona Low 2026) and rising coastal insurance costs

Capital deployment: $374M went into two acquisitions in October 2026 at roughly 13x EBITDA and is modelled as value-neutral (cash out, revenue in); the remaining ~$1.0B of pro-forma cash is netted against debt
Third-party operator (Marriott, Hyatt) execution on labour cost is outside Host's control

inputs.cash_note: Reported cash $1,492M at 30-Sep-2026 less the $138M Q3 regular dividend ($0.20, record date 30-Sep, paid 15-Oct-2026, accrued at the balance-sheet date) less $374M paid in October 2026 for 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge ($202M net of seller-funded FF&E) and Renaissance Dallas at Plano Legacy West ($172M) = $980M pro forma. The acquisitions' cash is deducted here because their revenue is now in the growth path (two months of FY2026, annualising in FY2027). Restricted cash / FF&E escrow ($159M) stays excluded: it funds the R&R capex already charged in the flows.
inputs.total_debt_note: Balance sheet 30-Sep-2026: senior notes 3,992 + credit facility incl. $1,000 term loans 999 + mortgage/other 93 = 5,084. The Metrics CSV TotalDebt (1,274 at FY2025) is the XBRL LongTermDebt subset tag, not total debt. $2.5B credit facility amended and restated 21-Oct-2026 (maturities to 2031-32, lower pricing, accordion $1.25B); weighted average maturity ~5.2y, weighted average rate ~4.8%, no drawings change.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: Unlevered pre-SBC owner FCF FY2025 = consolidated EBITDA 1,650 (operating profit 855 + D&A 795) - cash taxes 11.4 - total capex 724 (R&R + ROI, XBRL PaymentsForCapitalImprovements 282 + RealEstateImprovements 442). Company-basis levered FCF (OCF 1,510 - capex 724) = 786; the gap is interest paid 241 net of interest income and working-capital timing.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income sits below operating profit in Host's P&L, so the EBITDA the flows are built from (operating profit + D&A) already excludes it; nothing to strip. Cash is netted against debt in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement ShareBasedCompensation add-back $26M; the Adjusted EBITDAre and Adjusted FFO reconciliations use the same $26M (FY2026 forecast schedule, 5-Aug-2026 release). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed; SBC is 0.4% of revenue so the house/street band is negligible.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $205M; 9M-2026 $75M (4.0M shares at $18.97, all in H1; none in Q3); $405M authorisation remaining. Host is a repurchaser, so the flat share count is funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.share_count_basis: 687.3M = Q3-2026 diluted weighted-average share count (10-Q, 30-Sep-2026; basic 685.1M plus dilutive RSU/PSU; no Q3 repurchases or ATM issuance). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed. Host LP OP units held by third parties (9.2M units x 1.021494) are charged in the equity bridge at their 30-Sep-2026 redemption value ($211M) rather than added to the count.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Cost of equity 10.2% = 10y UST ~4.2% + beta 1.2 (lodging REIT; full hotel P&L exposure, operating leverage) x ERP 5.0%. Cost of debt 5.0% (4.8% weighted average on the stack, ~5.5% marginal on new unsecured notes); no tax shield because a REIT pays no entity-level tax. Weights at market: equity ~17.4B / debt 5.1B = 77/23. WACC = 0.77 x 10.2 + 0.23 x 5.0 = 9.0%. Unchanged from the 2026-09-29 build; the credit facility recast lowers the bank margin slightly but not the blended cost. Same WACC in all three scenarios - risk is charged once, through the probability weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating (ground) leases: US GAAP expenses the lease cost inside hotel operating costs, so it is already inside EBITDA (treatment A: cost in the flows). Lease liabilities ($563M) are therefore NOT added to net debt. lease_cost_pct_path is omitted (zero) to avoid charging the rent twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Redeemable non-controlling interests (Host LP OP units, $211M at 30-Sep-2026 redemption value) and non-redeemable NCI ($4M) are deducted in the equity bridge. Flows are consolidated, so this charges the NCI exactly once. Unconsolidated JV interests are excluded from the flows (equity in earnings sits below operating profit) and added back at book ($310M, advances to and investments in affiliates) - the matching-asset rule.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (unlevered, WACC, net debt deducted) - the SAME model as the 2026-09-29 build, deliberately NOT switched to AFFO-at-cost-of-equity. Reasons: (1) the SKILL's REIT row is for IAS-40 fair-value, externally-managed property trusts where net income is revaluation noise and the FCF inputs do not exist; Host is a US GAAP historical-cost, self-managed hotel owner whose revenue is the full hotel P&L, with real EBITDA (~27%), real capex (~9-10% of revenue) and real net debt on its own balance sheet. (2) Host's Adjusted FFO ($2.21/share guided) is PRE-capex; capitalising it at cost of equity would ignore ~$575M/yr of R&R and brand-mandated ROI capex. A FAD-at-CoE build (AFFO ~1,519 - capex ~575 = FAD ~944, $1.37/share; at CoE 10.2% and g 2.5% = ~$17.8/share) is the equivalent post-interest model and lands within a dollar of this DCF's base case, which is the cross-check. (3) The sector's valuation currency is EV/EBITDA, which is what an unlevered DCF implies. UPDATE 2026-11-19 (Q3-2026 10-Q, 4-Nov guidance raise): anchors refreshed to 30-Sep-2026 (price, pro-forma net debt 3,759 -> 4,104 after the Q3 dividend and $374M of October acquisitions, diluted shares 688.6 -> 687.3, JV book 299 -> 310, OP units 226 -> 211). Drivers re-judged: FY2026 only (all scenarios: revenue growth, EBITDA margin, capex %, D&A %) plus base FY2027 growth 3.0% -> 2.5%. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: every base/bull/bear growth, margin, SBC, capex, D&A and tax entry from FY2028 on, base FY2027 margin (27.1%), bull and bear FY2027 paths, WACC 9.0%, terminal growth, the 25/50/25 weights and the 15% hurdle. What would move them: initial FY2027 guidance (February 2027) outside RevPAR +1% to +3% or with comparable margin moving more than ~50bps; group booking pace for 2027-28 turning negative (bear weight up) or luxury rate growth holding above 4% without the World Cup (bull path); a capex re-base when the Marriott program scope is finalised; further acquisitions or a large disposition (net debt and revenue base together). REIT ADAPTATIONS: all capex (R&R + ROI) is charged - ROI projects are competitive/brand-mandated renovations, so their return is allowed only through the revenue growth path; cash tax stays at the TRS level (2.5% -> 5% of EBIT) permanently because REIT status is structural. CONVENTION: fy0 is FY2025 and year one is the full FY2026 flow, while net debt is the 30-Sep-2026 balance sheet; most of 9M-2026 FCF had already left as dividends ($1,007M paid YTD incl. the $0.72 special) so the overlap is small, and it is the same convention as the prior build. CYCLICALITY: lodging is the most cyclical REIT subsector (EBITDA margin 27% in FY2007 -> 18% in FY2009; FY2020 EBITDA negative). FY2026 is a guidance-boosted year (World Cup and America 250 in Q3, Maui recovery, $86M of low-margin condo revenue YTD), so the base case gives back margin in FY2027 rather than extrapolating, and the bear case is an explicit 2027-28 downturn. UNMODELLED: notes receivable and the remaining Four Seasons Orlando condo inventory are left out of the bridge (small upside); no further acquisitions assumed.
inputs.guidance_fy2026: 4-Nov-2026 (raised again): comparable hotel RevPAR ~+6.75% (was +4.75-5.25%), total RevPAR ~+6.0%; comparable hotel EBITDA margin ~30% (+80bps, was +40-50bps); Adjusted EBITDAre $1,865M (was $1,820-1,840M); net income $978M; diluted EPS $1.40; NAREIT FFO $2.17/share; Adjusted FFO $2.21/share (was $2.15-2.18); capex $550-600M (ROI 255-280, R&R 285-305, storm ~10-15; was 550-630), $392M spent through Q3. October comparable RevPAR ~+6.5%. No FY2027 guidance yet; STR/Tourism Economics see US RevPAR +1.5-2.5% in 2027. Total revenue is not in the 10-Q: modelled at ~$6,255M (9M actual 4,632 incl. $86M condo sales + Q4 ~1,620: Q4-2025 1,603, ~+6% total RevPAR offset by ~6% of disposed revenue, plus ~$15M from the two October acquisitions).

bear.rationale: FY2026 just short of guidance (+2.1%, 27.2%), then a 2027-28 lodging downturn: revenue -8% and -4% with EBITDA margin compressing to 22% through operating leverage (calibrated to FY2007-09, when Host's revenue fell 21% and margin fell from 27% to 18%; this bear is roughly half that severity). Capex is deferred but brand standards limit the cut. Recovery FY2029-31 back to 26% margin - structurally higher labour and insurance costs. Terminal growth 2.0%. All entries from FY2027 on UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-29 build; the stronger 2026 raises the level the downturn starts from, not its shape.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +2.3% = ~$6,255M (was +0.4% / $6,138M at the August guidance): comparable RevPAR raised to +6.75%, $86M of condo revenue YTD and two months of the October acquisitions, against the Four Seasons and other disposals. FY2027 +2.5% (was 3.0%): organic ~+2.0% (STR 1.5-2.5%, lapping World Cup/America 250 and the Maui recovery, on a base 1.75pts of RevPAR higher than assumed in September) + ~1.2pts from annualising Brooklyn Bridge and Plano - ~0.7pts from the Q1-2026 Four Seasons months dropping out. FY2028-30 +3.0% and the fade to 2.5% are UNCHANGED.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 27.4% (was 27.3%): 9M EBITDA 1,303 (operating profit 733 + D&A 570) plus Q4 ~415 = ~1,718 on ~6,255; equivalently the prior 1,676 plus the $35M Adjusted EBITDAre raise. The margin rises only 10bps despite the raise because the $86M of condo revenue carries a ~17% margin. FY2027 27.1% UNCHANGED - a 30bps give-back as RevPAR of ~2% runs below wage growth and Q3's event-driven flow-through laps. ~27% thereafter UNCHANGED (FY2019 27.0%, FY2025 27.0%).
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 9.2% = $575M guidance midpoint (range narrowed to 550-600 from 550-630) on ~6,255. 10.0% FY2027-29 while the Marriott transformational program runs ($300-350M through 2029) and Hyatt completes in 2027, 9.5% thereafter - UNCHANGED.
base.tax_rationale: REIT: only TRS income is taxed. Cash taxes paid were $11-12M/yr FY2023-25 (~1.3% of EBIT); GAAP provision guided $52-54M for FY2026 (~5.5% incl. $5M on dispositions). Path 2.5% -> 5% of EBIT is between the two. Held permanently - REIT status is structural, not a carryforward to ramp to 21%. UNCHANGED (9M-2026 income taxes paid $18M, ~2.5% of EBIT, on the path).
base.da_rationale: FY2026 12.2% = ~$760M (9M 570, Q3 187) on ~6,255. Later years UNCHANGED. Only affects the flows via the ~3-5% cash tax rate.

bull.rationale: FY2026 slightly above guidance (+2.5%, 27.5%), then the expansion extends: luxury/upper-upscale RevPAR compounds 4-5% on rate with group pace strong and no new supply (FY2027 +5.0% now also carries ~0.5pt net from the October acquisitions), renovated Hyatt/Marriott assets earn their RevPAR premium, and margins expand ~110bps to 28.5% as rate outruns wages. Capex normalises toward 9% once both transformational programs finish. Terminal growth 3.0%. All entries from FY2027 on UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-29 build.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: lodging is the most cyclical REIT subsector, the expansion is six years old, and FY2026 guidance embeds transitory tailwinds (World Cup, Maui base effect, condo sales) that make 2027 comparisons hard. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs sustained 4-5% rate growth AND margin expansion against wage inflation AND a multiple re-rating, three independent things. Base 50%. UNCHANGED at the 2026-11-19 update: the Q3 beat and raise is evidence about 2026, not about the cycle; the absence of FY2027 guidance and consensus deceleration to +1.5-2.5% RevPAR are already what the base path assumes.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
